rv.q: I should note at this point that the cast of this excellent and unstinting premiere from Chicago director Azar Kazemi is made up entirely of adults, including several superb recent college graduates.
Despite the uniformly fine cast and Kazemi's sharp direction, there are times when it feels like the story is spinning its wheels a bit.
This play, while full of excellent artistry, left me unsatisfied.
The script needs work to explore Hamed's story, which is especially relevant today, and to differentiate the student characters and their own stories.

cn.t: Salem's searing drama about Catholic Church abuse earns praise for its bold subject matter but divides critics, with some finding it lacks the warmth of his earlier work and needs further development of its Palestinian-American storyline.
